metadata.title: Lesson 1: Annotating the client brief
metadata.summary: Use the Oakfield scenario to identify the client, users, current situation, problems, requirements and constraints.

metadata.title: Lesson 2: Market, problems and risks
metadata.summary: Look beyond the brief: market context, problems with the current approach, and risks if nothing changes.

metadata.title: Lesson 3: Current systems and exit check
metadata.summary: Investigate current hardware, software and practice, then close the week with remaining unknowns.

metadata.title: Homework: one real digital product
metadata.summary: Analyse one real digital product or service using the same headings you used on the Oakfield brief.

metadata.title: Lesson 1: Existing versus emerging options
metadata.summary: Retrieve Week 1 findings, then compare an existing approach with an emerging alternative.

metadata.title: Lesson 2: Evaluate candidate solutions
metadata.summary: Evaluate two or three candidates for Oakfield, including at least one emerging technology.

metadata.title: Lesson 3: Regulation and knowledge gaps
metadata.summary: Identify guidelines or regulations that may apply, and list personal knowledge, skill or information gaps.

metadata.title: Homework: one emerging technology with a source
metadata.summary: Research one emerging technology relevant to Oakfield. Note one benefit, one risk and one source.

metadata.title: Lesson 1: From research to scoped requirements
metadata.summary: Turn a vague client statement into a scoped requirement, with in-scope, out-of-scope and unknown.

metadata.title: Lesson 2: Decomposition, patterns and abstraction
metadata.summary: Break the Oakfield problem into parts, group similar needs and drop unnecessary detail.

metadata.title: Lesson 3: First-cut scope statement
metadata.summary: Produce a first-cut scope statement and a simple decomposition for the continuing scenario.

metadata.title: Homework: rewrite two vague statements
metadata.summary: Rewrite two vague client statements as clearer business requirements and mark whether each is in scope.

metadata.title: Lesson 1: Need, feature, constraint or unknown
metadata.summary: Retrieve the Week 3 scope and classify sample statements.

metadata.title: Lesson 2: Testable wording
metadata.summary: Classify realistic statements and rewrite weak examples so they are testable.

metadata.title: Lesson 3: Labelled requirements list
metadata.summary: Produce a short requirements list labelled functional, non-functional, constraint, KPI or acceptance.

metadata.title: Homework: acceptance for everyday actions
metadata.summary: Write acceptance criteria for two everyday digital actions, such as logging in or making a payment.

metadata.title: Lesson 1: Milestone plan
metadata.summary: Retrieve scoped requirements and draft a milestone schedule that includes testing and client review.

metadata.title: Lesson 2: Resources and a costed outline
metadata.summary: Allocate people, time and other resources; produce a simple costed outline for an early increment.

metadata.title: Lesson 3: Language and stack choice
metadata.summary: Recommend a language or stack against suitability, policy, scalability, security, staffing, cost and reliability.

metadata.title: Homework: public project overruns
metadata.summary: Compare two public project overruns in the news and identify whether the issue looks like scope, schedule, resource or cost.

metadata.title: Lesson 1: Risk records
metadata.summary: Identify people, technology, schedule, data, supplier and user risks; distinguish mitigation from contingency.

metadata.title: Lesson 2: User stories and activity diagrams
metadata.summary: Produce stories and an activity diagram for at least two user groups.

metadata.title: Lesson 3: Mind map and now/next/later road map
metadata.summary: Draft a mind map of the problem space and a product road map that respects scope and highest-value stories.

metadata.title: Homework: stories for a familiar service
metadata.summary: Write two user stories for a familiar college or public service and note who is not represented.

metadata.title: Lesson 1: Process diagram and first-cut ERD
metadata.summary: Retrieve the priority user journey and model process plus data.

metadata.title: Lesson 2: Interface sketch and algorithm
metadata.summary: Create a low-fidelity interface for a priority task and plan the algorithm behind it.

metadata.title: Lesson 3: Data-requirement design versus acceptance
metadata.summary: Plan data fields and check the design against acceptance criteria.

metadata.title: Homework: critique a public screen
metadata.summary: Critique one public website or app screen against a user need and suggest one interface improvement.

metadata.title: Lesson 1: What a prototype must prove
metadata.summary: Retrieve a Week 7 design decision and identify what a prototype would need to prove to the client.

metadata.title: Lesson 2: Reviewing AI-generated output
metadata.summary: Review a supplied AI fragment for correctness, security, bias, licensing and fit to requirements.

metadata.title: Lesson 3: Evaluate the prototype plan
metadata.summary: Record what you would keep, change or reject and state one prototype question the client could answer.

metadata.title: Homework: AI policy or AI error
metadata.summary: Find an organisation's public statement on acceptable AI use, or a news example of AI error, and note one implication for software teams.

metadata.title: Lesson 1: Test levels
metadata.summary: Map module, integration, automated and user testing onto the lifecycle.

metadata.title: Lesson 2: Automated tests, user tests and feedback
metadata.summary: Plan automated and user testing and how feedback would be gathered.

metadata.title: Lesson 3: Deploy, install, configure, update
metadata.summary: Outline go-live steps including who does what.

metadata.title: Homework: how a familiar app updates
metadata.summary: Describe how a familiar app updates and what users are asked to do, then note one support or training implication.

metadata.title: Lesson 1: Version control as a professional story
metadata.summary: A change, a commit message, why history matters, and a live bug.

metadata.title: Lesson 2: Maintenance, support, training, updates
metadata.summary: Map maintenance activities onto the client scenario.

metadata.title: Lesson 3: Why the SDLC adds organisational value
metadata.summary: Explain SDLC value using the continuing project.

metadata.title: Homework: the last update you noticed
metadata.summary: Describe the last update you noticed on a familiar service and who had to be informed or trained.

metadata.title: Lesson 1: Who owns each SDLC stage
metadata.summary: Retrieve SDLC stages and meet the first official role set.

metadata.title: Lesson 2: Project manager responsibilities
metadata.summary: Budget, scope, schedule, risk and quality.

metadata.title: Lesson 3: Analyst, designer, and assigning the increment
metadata.summary: Assign the first role set to one Oakfield increment.

metadata.title: Homework: job advertisement
metadata.summary: Research one job advertisement for a digital role from this week's set and list the responsibilities that match the specification.

metadata.title: Lesson 1: Developer, operations and security
metadata.summary: Who writes code, who keeps a service running, who owns security.

metadata.title: Lesson 2: Tester and quality assurance
metadata.summary: Software tester and QA responsibilities.

metadata.title: Lesson 3: Sprint, epic, story, spike
metadata.summary: Write one epic, one user story and one spike for an uncertainty.

metadata.title: Homework: sprint review or stand-up
metadata.summary: Find one public description of a sprint review or stand-up and note what artefact was being discussed.

metadata.title: Lesson 1: Agile incremental delivery
metadata.summary: Map changing requirements and client feedback onto an incremental plan.

metadata.title: Lesson 2: Scaled Agile and product increments
metadata.summary: When more than one team must align.

metadata.title: Lesson 3: Waterfall and a justified choice
metadata.summary: When Waterfall documentation and staged client interaction might still be justified.

metadata.title: Homework: a delayed digital project
metadata.summary: Find a public case of a delayed digital project and suggest whether a fixed plan or changing requirements contributed.

metadata.title: Lesson 1: RAD
metadata.summary: Prototyping, reuse and when RAD is suitable.

metadata.title: Lesson 2: Lean
metadata.summary: Waste reduction, late decisions and short iterations.

metadata.title: Lesson 3: Compare and select
metadata.summary: Compare Agile, Scaled Agile, Waterfall, RAD and Lean; write a client-readable justification.

metadata.title: Homework: waste in a familiar process
metadata.summary: Identify one waste in a familiar process, such as repeated data entry, and suggest a shorter iteration that would reduce it.

metadata.title: Lesson 1: UCD characteristics
metadata.summary: Retrieve methodology and mark which requirements protect users or data.

metadata.title: Lesson 2: UCD stages on Oakfield
metadata.summary: Apply context, requirements, design and assessment.

metadata.title: Lesson 3: Secure by design in functional requirements
metadata.summary: Write or improve one FR and one acceptance check so security is designed in.

metadata.title: Homework: public login or form
metadata.summary: Review one public login or form against UCD and note one security or accessibility gap.

metadata.title: Lesson 1: Security, accessibility, scalability NFR
metadata.summary: Retrieve missing quality requirements and write NFR with matching acceptance.

metadata.title: Lesson 2: KPIs versus acceptance criteria
metadata.summary: KPIs for responsiveness, load handling and reliability.

metadata.title: Lesson 3: Plan a spike
metadata.summary: Time-boxed investigation to reduce a technical unknown.

metadata.title: Homework: rewrite vague quality statements
metadata.summary: Rewrite two vague quality statements, such as fast or user-friendly, so they can be checked.

metadata.title: Lesson 1: IoT, AI, generative AI, ML
metadata.summary: Structured technology profiles; AI is not a single technology.

metadata.title: Lesson 2: Vision, biometrics, robotics
metadata.summary: Object recognition, computer vision, biometrics, robotics — data, risk, user impact.

metadata.title: Lesson 3: Cloud, data, drones, 3D, 5G — scoped recommendations
metadata.summary: Recommend now, later or reject for each profiled technology.

metadata.title: Homework: sources on one profile
metadata.summary: Add sources to one technology profile and note how recent and independent those sources are.

metadata.title: Lesson 1: Personal training plan
metadata.summary: Identify knowledge, skill and ability gaps.

metadata.title: Lesson 2: Legal, regulatory, ethical, risk
metadata.summary: Investigate one requirement that applies to the client.

metadata.title: Lesson 3: Sources and qualitative / quantitative evaluation
metadata.summary: Rate sources; choose one qualitative and one quantitative method.

metadata.title: Homework: two sources on the same topic
metadata.summary: Evaluate two sources on the same legal or technology topic and write which you would trust more in a proposal, and why.

metadata.title: Lesson 1: SDLC retrieval and common errors
metadata.summary: Repair common errors in SDLC sequence and role responsibilities.

metadata.title: Lesson 2: Roles recap on the scenario
metadata.summary: Match roles to a project scenario.

metadata.title: Lesson 3: One-page recap
metadata.summary: Produce a one-page SDLC and roles recap for the continuing client project.

metadata.title: Homework: revise one weak artefact
metadata.summary: Revise one weak piece of earlier project evidence, such as a brief annotation or role assignment.

metadata.title: Lesson 1: Methodology comparison task
metadata.summary: Justify a methodology with context, not a label.

metadata.title: Lesson 2: Rewrite a weak requirement and a weak technology recommendation
metadata.summary: UCD, secure-by-design, reject fashionable tech that does not fit.

metadata.title: Lesson 3: Update the training plan
metadata.summary: Update against gaps still showing in revision.

metadata.title: Homework: one recent source on a technology profile
metadata.summary: Add one recent source to an emerging-technology profile.

metadata.title: Lesson 1: Legal and ethical scenarios
metadata.summary: Distinguish law, regulation, ethics and software standards.

metadata.title: Lesson 2: Risk register, CIA, continuity
metadata.summary: Owners and monitoring, not just a risk name.

metadata.title: Lesson 3: Source grid and evaluation methods
metadata.summary: More than a single blog post; qualitative and quantitative.

metadata.title: Homework: two sources on a legal topic
metadata.summary: Evaluate two sources on the same legal topic and write which you would trust in a proposal, and why.

metadata.title: Lesson 1: Cumulative retrieval and Task 1 structure
metadata.summary: How Task 1 draws on Areas 1 to 3 together, without providing assessed responses.

metadata.title: Lesson 2: Timed integrated case study
metadata.summary: Requirements and risk together, then peer-assess against acceptance criteria.

metadata.title: Lesson 3: Readiness checklist and placement
metadata.summary: Final assessment-readiness checklist and one remaining personal training need.

metadata.title: Homework: organise the evidence pack
metadata.summary: Organise your research log, requirements list, models and source list so they can be reused under assessment conditions according to centre rules.
